items.stem: In an integrated three-statement model, net income links to which balance-sheet line?

options.rationale: Correct: net income (less dividends) accumulates in retained earnings.
Payables track supplier obligations, not accumulated profit.
Fixed assets change with capex and depreciation, not net income directly.
Share capital changes with equity issuance, not retained profit.

items.explanation: Correct: net income (less dividends) accumulates in retained earnings.

items.stem: Why is a balance check (assets = liabilities + equity) included in a model?

options.text: To flag immediately when the statements no longer tie out
options.rationale: Correct: the check surfaces linking errors as soon as the balance sheet stops balancing.

options.text: To calculate the company's tax bill
options.rationale: Tax is computed on the income statement, not by the balance check.
Revenue is driven by assumptions, not the balance check.

options.text: To format the output for printing
options.rationale: The check is a control, not a formatting tool.

items.explanation: Correct: the check surfaces linking errors as soon as the balance sheet stops balancing.

items.stem: Which TWO are good spreadsheet-modeling practices? (Select TWO)

options.text: Keep assumptions in clearly labelled input cells separate from formulas
options.rationale: Correct: separating inputs from calculations makes a model auditable and flexible.

options.text: Build error checks that flag when the model fails to balance
options.rationale: Correct: automated checks catch linking mistakes early.

options.text: Hardcode constants inside formulas so they cannot be changed
options.rationale: Hardcoding hides assumptions and makes updates error-prone.

options.text: Avoid documenting any assumption so the model stays compact
options.rationale: Undocumented assumptions make a model hard to trust or reuse.

items.explanation: Correct: separating inputs from calculations makes a model auditable and flexible.; Correct: automated checks catch linking mistakes early.
